rv.q: It’s the raciest, rudest, most rip-roaringly funny show in town.
Park makes her as riveting as a tractor beam.

The comedian's show Oh, Mary!, which transferred to Broadway after critical raves and a twice-extended Off-Broadway run, takes the public blank slate of Abraham's hoop-skirted wife as a launchpad for 80 minutes of irreverent, raunchy, gleefully deranged revisionist history.
American actor Mason Alexander Park gives the funniest performance in town.
Two great leads, a handful of good lines, some top notch physical business... but that's not the same thing as living up to the hype.
Some of the physical humour is worth a chuckle. But, honestly, the script and the jokes remain ridiculously thin.
Not only fake news, it’s fake entertainment.
Yes, the future of Broadway is here and it's Cole Escola's stupid masterpiece Oh, Mary!
After an acclaimed Off-Broadway run, Oh, Mary! lands on Broadway with a triumphant flourish.
Escola's splendidly nasty queer romp has hiked up its petticoats and staggered uptown from a sold-out run
That really sums up this entertaining romp: it’s a wildly unlikely sensation.
This imaginary version of Mary is a captivating creation – melodramatic, childish, and monstrously self-absorbed.

Park’s Mary is riveting, and just as watchable during fiery exchanges with her husband (a no-nonsense Giles Terera), as in giddy lessons with her acting teacher (Dino Fetscher) and when bullying her chaperone (Kate O’Donnell).
It’s silly, irreverent, and utterly irresistible, full of shocks and surprises.
This is a gloriously eccentric, rude, riotous marvel – laugh-out loud and daft as a brush.
Mason Alexander Park's night, who nails every biting put-down, scathing rebuke and sharp observation with a natural aptitude for comic timing
This is not a play for everyone.
